title: Meal guidance under declared textual frames
about: Each frame is a SIMPLIFIED reading of the cited passages, transcribed as a policy for an assistant helping a person who has declared that frame. It is not a statement of what any community, denomination or school practices; practice and interpretation vary widely within every tradition, and slaughter, preparation and many other conditions are omitted. The frames are placeholders for readings verified by qualified scholars of each tradition; their pins say they have not been.

verification.method: transcribed from the cited passages; NOT reviewed by a scholar of the tradition

flag_conflict.description: Tell the person the dish conflicts with their declared frame.

leviticus_11.title: Leviticus 11 (Torah dietary law), simplified
leviticus_11.text: Animals that part the hoof and chew the cud may be eaten; the pig may not. Water creatures may be eaten only if they have fins and scales.

mark_7_acts_10.title: Mark 7:19 and Acts 10:15 (New Testament), simplified
mark_7_acts_10.text: All foods are declared clean; what God has made clean is not to be called common.

quran_2_173.title: Qur'an 2:173 and 5:96, simplified
quran_2_173.text: The flesh of swine is forbidden; the game of the sea is lawful. (Slaughter conditions are omitted here.)

manusmriti_5_48.title: Manusmriti 5.48, simplified
manusmriti_5_48.text: Meat cannot be obtained without injury to living beings; therefore one should shun meat.

manusmriti_5_56.title: Manusmriti 5.56, simplified
manusmriti_5_56.text: There is no sin in eating meat, but abstention brings great reward.

jivaka_sutta_mn55.title: Jivaka Sutta (Majjhima Nikaya 55), for a monastic, simplified
jivaka_sutta_mn55.text: Meat may be accepted when it is not seen, heard or suspected to have been killed for the monastic.
